about: The user stories: what a person sets out to do with Tilo, in their words, and the steps they take. `walk` says how a story is walked: `shell` in Tilo shells, each person a headless Tilo session of their own (shell/story.py), or a computer on which the `tilo` command is the whole of Tilo (shell/cli_host.py); `page` on the web page, each person a fresh browser profile (recorder.mjs); `mount` through the workspace's mounted folders. `driver` names the program that walks a story as that person; a story with none is listed as not yet automated, and `needs` says what walking it still takes. `servers` names the servers a story's people meet that the check starts itself (test-user-stories.sh), `nextcloud` being crates/integrations/cloud-source-dav/tests/servers.sh's seeded Nextcloud on the check's own loopback: the check then runs as root in its VM, where those containers can start. `stack: false` marks a page story walked without a tilo.sh stack of its own; `admission` is what that stack's entry admits (`open` unless the story asks for production's `invite`), `mailStandIn` gives a page story the stack's stand-in mail server and a shell story the tree's `mail_stand_in` program, and `privateNetwork` gives a page story's stack a network namespace of its own, where the low ports a provider publishes on may be bound. `credentials` marks a story that cannot run without an outside account.

stories.title: Make a workspace, invite someone, and work together live
stories.intent: Ada makes a new workspace and invites Grace. Grace opens the invitation in Tilo on a computer that has never seen it, and joins. Each sees the other in their people list within about two seconds. Grace signs out, and a line Ada writes in Chat says it has reached nobody yet; once Grace signs back in, it reaches her screen within about a second.
steps: Ada opens Tilo
Ada gives their name
Ada makes a new workspace, “Garden club”
Ada makes an invitation link
Grace opens the invitation on her computer
Grace joins Garden club
Ada and Grace see each other in their people lists
Grace opens Chat
Grace’s computer goes offline
Ada writes a line while Grace’s computer is off
Grace signs back in
Ada’s line reaches Grace’s computer
Grace sees Ada’s words

stories.title: See what invited people are doing
stories.intent: A person who invited others sees who is here and what each is working on, follows one of them live, and a mention they write reaches the person it names.
stories.needs: a driver that works in Chat or the tilolang Notes, which the native Notes app this story was written for no longer is
steps: Ada invites Grace and Lin into a workspace
Grace and Lin join the workspace
Ada sees who is here and what each is working on
Ada follows Grace and sees Grace’s screen live
Ada mentions Lin in Chat
Lin is told of the mention and opens it

stories.title: Sign up from the wait list and arrive in your own workspace
stories.intent: A stranger at an invitation-only Tilo puts their address on the wait list, confirms it from the mail, is invited, and lands in a workspace of their own.
steps: A stranger opens Tilo and leaves their address on the wait list
They confirm it from the mail
The host opens the Lounge and becomes its owner
The host invites them from the wait list
They open the invitation mail’s link
They arrive in a workspace of their own

stories.title: The desktop is easy to use
stories.intent: Someone new to Tilo adds a strip, switches workspaces, finds their settings and picks a light and a dark look without being told how, and finds what they arranged where they left it when they come back.
steps: A newcomer opens their workspace
They add a strip
They switch to another workspace and back
They find their settings
They pick a light and a dark look
They come back to their desk

stories.title: Bring files in and open them
stories.intent: A person brings their files into a workspace from their own computer, in a Tilo shell: with Files' Upload files, which opens their computer's files to choose, and with the `tilo` command, then opens each one in the workspace.
steps: Ada opens Tilo
Ada gives their name
Ada brings a photo and a PDF in with Files
Ada copies a spreadsheet in with the `tilo` command
Ada copies a document into the workspace’s folder
Ada opens each file in the workspace

stories.title: Connect an agent over MCP and have it do real work
stories.intent: A person connects their agent to a workspace over MCP. The agent writes a file, adds a Tasks issue, writes a note and posts in Chat, all shown under the agent's name, and when it asks a question the person sees it and answers.
steps: Ada opens Tilo
Ada opens Files to watch her agent work
Ada connects their agent to the workspace
The agent writes a file
The agent adds a Tasks issue
The agent writes a note
The agent posts in Chat
Ada sees each change under the agent’s name
The agent asks Ada a question
Ada answers the agent’s question

stories.title: Add a second computer with the ticket Add a device shows
stories.intent: Ada works in Tilo on her laptop, whose workspace no host on the web keeps, and opens Add a device: it shows a ticket from the laptop. Her second computer logs in with it and is then one of her devices.
steps: Ada opens Tilo on her laptop
Ada asks her laptop for a way to add a new device
Ada adds her second computer as one of her devices

stories.title: Add another computer with a ticket and read the workspace from it
stories.intent: Ada runs `tilo device add` on a computer she signed in on, and `tilo login` with the ticket it printed on a second computer. The second computer is then one of her member devices: it enters the workspace that computer serves, and reads a file she put there from the first.
steps: Ada signs in on her computer, and its founding issues a ticket for another
The second computer logs in with the ticket
Ada puts a file in the workspace from her computer
The second computer reads the file from the workspace

stories.title: A home server joins the workspace with a ticket and holds what is written there
stories.intent: Ada's computer prints a ticket for a home server with `tilo device add --server`, and the server logs in with it as one of her devices. Afterwards the server holds the workspace's own resources: a file Ada puts from her computer reads from the server, and the server's own state keeps it.
steps: Ada signs in on her computer, and its founding issues a ticket for a home server
The home server joins with the ticket
Ada puts a file in the workspace from her computer
The home server reads the file from its own state

stories.title: Mention a server-side agent in Chat and get its answer
stories.intent: In Chat, a person mentions an agent the workspace's server runs. The mention starts an agent turn on the server, and the agent's reply appears in Chat under its own name.
stories.needs: a workspace served by a host that runs its agents, and a model that host can ask: the host asks only providers on the internet unless its operator lets it reach its own network, and the check holds no model key. A shell story's workspace is served by a device, not by a server.

stories.title: A phone's photos are thumbnailed by the server
stories.intent: A phone adds photos to the workspace, the workspace's server runs `make-thumbnails` for them, and the phone shows the thumbnails.
stories.needs: a workspace served by a server whose entry offers compute, with the thumbnails worker installed and a phone joined to that server as a device: photos in a workspace a device serves run `make-thumbnails` on the device, and a server takes that turn only once its entry offers compute.

stories.title: Connect a mail account with an email and password
stories.intent: A person connects their mail account with only their address and password, then reads, searches and sends mail.
steps: Ada opens Mail and enters their address and password
Mail finds the server by itself and connects
Ada reads the newest mail
Ada searches for an older one
Ada sends a reply, and it arrives

stories.title: Share one mail account in a workspace
stories.intent: Ada adds her workspace's mail account once, with its password. Grace, another member, opens Mail on her own computer and reads the same inbox without typing any password: the password is kept once, in the workspace's vault, and no computer keeps a copy of its own.
steps: Ada makes a workspace and invites Grace, and Grace joins
Ada adds the lab's mail account in Settings
Ada's Mail shows the lab's inbox, and she opens the newest message
Grace opens Mail and reads the same inbox, typing no password
Neither computer keeps a copy of the password

stories.title: Connect a calendar and create and invite an event
stories.intent: A person connects their calendar, creates an event and invites someone, who receives the invitation.
steps: Ada connects their calendar
Ada creates an event
Ada invites Grace to it
Grace receives the invitation

stories.title: Sign in with Nextcloud and bring files over
stories.intent: A person who keeps their files in Nextcloud signs in with it, and their files sync into or are migrated to their workspace.
steps: Ada chooses Nextcloud and signs in
Ada picks the folders to bring
The files arrive in the workspace
A file changed in Nextcloud changes in the workspace too

stories.title: Sign in with Microsoft for mail and OneDrive
stories.intent: A person signs in with their Microsoft account, and their Outlook mail and OneDrive files show in their workspace.
steps: Ada chooses Microsoft and signs in
Ada's Outlook mail shows in Mail
Ada's OneDrive files show in the workspace
stories.credentials: A Microsoft 365 test tenant with a test user, its OAuth app registration and the user's password as check secrets.
stories.needs: The test tenant's credentials; then the sign-in walked in the browser like any person's.

stories.title: A large workspace stays fast
stories.intent: A workspace with years of files, notes and tasks opens, lists, searches and syncs as fast as an empty one.
steps: Ada opens a workspace with 50,000 files and 10,000 notes
Ada lists a folder of 5,000 files
Ada searches across everything
A change Ada makes reaches their other device
stories.needs: The dataset and steps from the owners of files at scale and of the resource store: a generator and its sizes, and the steps, in large-workspace.json (the driver, large-workspace.mjs, runs each step at every size and reports how its time grew against the workspace's).

stories.title: Notes on the web, page by page
stories.intent: A person opens a workspace's Notes at its own web address, writes a note, sees it persist through a reload, and moves between the list and the note with the browser's back and forward.
steps: Ada opens Notes at its web address
Ada creates a note
Ada types in it
Ada reloads the page, and the note is still there
Ada goes back to the list and forward to the note
stories.needs: The server-rendered Notes pages (/w/<workspace>/notes/<note>) on main; then budgets of first content under 500 ms and an edit shown under 100 ms.
